rhea_intro.title: The Protocol
rhea_intro.narrator: Rhea Solys. Commander. What she chose to tell.
rhea_intro.text:
A protocol is not a prison.

It is a net.

You weave it before the fall, not during.

I spent eleven years learning that, before taking command of Aletheia-9.

Eleven years believing that if I followed every rule, to the letter, no one under my orders would be lost.

rhea_devoir.title: Eleven Years of Silence
rhea_devoir.text:
Before Aletheia-9, I lost a man under my command. Another station, another life.

A procedural error. Mine.

Since then, I leave nothing to chance.

My crew finds me cold. Rigid. Perhaps.

But none of my crews ever lost anyone. Until that night.

rhea_nuit_debut.title: 02:00 — Command Center
rhea_nuit_debut.text:
That night, I was making my usual control rounds. Nothing out of the ordinary.

Dorian was on routine maintenance, sector 4. Maya was working late on her cell cultures, as always.

Léo was running an electrical wiring check, scheduled three days in advance.

An ordinary night. I would have sworn it.

rhea_alerte.title: 02:13 — The Alarm
rhea_alerte.text:
The red alarm sounded at exactly 02:13. Micro-outage in sector 4, then silence from Léo's radio.

ORIS could no longer locate his transponder.

In eleven years, I had never seen this kind of failure.

My first reflex was the lockdown protocol. Always the protocol.

choices.text: You followed the protocol to the letter.
You hesitated, one second too long.

rhea_lockdown.title: Partial Lockdown
rhea_lockdown.text:
I ordered a partial lockdown of sector 4, time to assess the threat.

Dorian wanted to go down immediately, without waiting for my go-ahead.

I held him back. The protocol exists for this: not to send a second person to get lost while searching for the first.

He never forgave me for it, I think.

rhea_conflit_dorian.title: A Disagreement
rhea_conflit_dorian.text:
*"We're wasting time!"*, he shouted at me.

*"We're not wasting anything. We're avoiding losing two."*, I replied.

He clenched his fists, but he stayed. As always.

Three minutes later, I lifted the lockdown and went down myself, with Maya.

choices.text: You were treating him like a suspect.

rhea_deplacement.title: Descent to Sector 4
rhea_deplacement.text:
The trip took four minutes. Maya said nothing, focused, almost too calm for the situation.

The sector's neon lights still flickered intermittently.

A smell of burnt circuitry hung in the air, stronger than it should have been for a simple micro-outage.

choices.text: You left the post anyway despite protocol.

rhea_scene_vide.title: Nothing
rhea_scene_vide.text:
The maintenance panel was open. Léo's tools on the floor, neatly arranged.

Too neatly arranged for someone in the middle of an emergency.

No sign of a struggle. No sign of exit. No sign of him, period.

For the first time in eleven years, I felt that protocol might not be enough.

rhea_soupcon.title: A Matter of Procedure
rhea_soupcon.text:
It was not an accident. An accident leaves a mess. Here, everything was too clean.

I thought of Dorian, of his anger at not being allowed down right away. Of Maya, so calm, almost absent.

I thought of myself too, of that minute of lockdown that may have cost a life.

A good commander considers every hypothesis. Even the worst. Even her own.

choices.text: You wonder if it's your fault.

rhea_reflexion_dorian.title: The Nervous One
rhea_reflexion_dorian.text:
Dorian panics easily. He improvises, he breaks rules when it suits him.

That is not proof. I know. But eleven years of command teach you to spot who cracks first.

That night, he cracked before I even went down.

rhea_secret.title: What I Never Reported
rhea_secret.text:
Six months ago, a technical report flagged instability in sector 4's electrical grid.

I classified it as minor. I did not want another audit on my record, so close to my promotion.

I did not think it would come back to haunt me like this.

If I had escalated that report... maybe Léo would still be here.

choices.text: That report should have been filed.

rhea_conclusion.title: My Version
rhea_conclusion.text:
Here is what I know: someone, or something, made Léo Kanek vanish at 02:13, in a sector I knew was unstable and chose to keep quiet about.

I cannot tell you who. Or what.

But I can tell you that protocol, that night, was not enough. And that is my responsibility.

fin_recit_rhea.title: End of Account
fin_recit_rhea.text: Rhea's account ends. She watches you, almost relieved to have finally spoken.
